title: Check yourself: The team setup: where each instruction lives

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A team wants a review command that every developer has after cloning the repository. Where does the file go?

options.text: In a settings file that holds a list of commands for Claude Code
options.says: Ruled out because no such mechanism exists: "A `commands` array in a config file is a mechanism that does not exist".

options.text: In a commands folder in each developer's home directory, created by hand
options.says: Ruled out because a home folder is personal: "commands in the home folder are personal".

options.text: In the root instructions file, under a heading that names the review checklist
options.says: Ruled out because the memory file holds instructions and not definitions: "the memory file is for instructions and context".

options.text: In the project's own configuration folder, committed with the sources
options.says: A command file in the project's own folder is committed and reaches every clone.

questions.stem: An audit of a team's setup prints `test-uncovered`. What does that finding report?

options.text: A file of tests that no rule reaches
options.says: The finding is the colocated-tests question: "`test-uncovered`: a test file that no rule reaches, which is the colocated-tests question of the exam."

options.text: A rule whose globs match none of the project's files
options.says: Ruled out because that is another finding: "a rule with no `paths` list, or whose globs match none of the project's files".

options.text: A root file with several sections and no rule files
options.says: Ruled out for the same reason: "three or more sections in the root file and no rule files".

options.text: A project with no command file and no skill
options.says: Ruled out as a third finding: "no command file and no skill in the project".

origin.section: The audit: a checklist that reads the files

questions.stem: In the fixed project, a spec file beside a handler gets two sets of conventions. Why?

options.text: A skill for each area starts as soon as the path matches
options.says: Ruled out because a path starts no skill: "a skill is invoked, or chosen by the model from its description, and a path match does not start it".

options.text: The root file lists every rule that applies to a spec
options.says: Ruled out because the root file is for "What every task needs: the test command, the repository's etiquette", kept short, and not a list of rules by kind of file.

options.text: Its area's rule and the testing rule both have globs that match its path
options.says: Both rules have a glob that matches the path. The page says the spec files "load two rule files each: the rule of their area and the testing rule".

options.text: Every rule loads as soon as the first file of the session is opened
options.says: Ruled out because a rule waits for a matching file: "A rule with a `paths` list loads when Claude works with a file that matches one of its globs".
